requirements.original: The set of keys that the map associates with a value can be accessed using the from selector.
requirements.canonical: The set of keys that a map associates with a value MAY be accessed using the `from` selector.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.15.5 -- The set of keys that the map associates with a value can be accessed using the from selector.

requirements.original: _MapValue "." from_
requirements.canonical: The `from` selector on a map value has the syntax MapValue "." `from`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.15.5 -- _MapValue "." from_

requirements.original: _MapValueType_ "." `from`
requirements.canonical: The `from` selector on a map type has the syntax MapValueType "." `from`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.15.5 -- _MapValueType_ "." `from`

requirements.original: If the MapValue is a value of type MapValueType defined as map from _A_ to _B_ then MapValue.from yields a result compatible with type set of A that contains all the key values from MapValue.
requirements.canonical: If MapValue is a value of a type defined as `map from` A `to` B, then MapValue.from yields a result compatible with type `set of` A that contains all key values of MapValue.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.15.5 -- If the MapValue is a value of type MapValueType defined as map from _A_ to _B_ then MapValue.from yields a result compatible with type set of A that contains all the key values from MapValue.

requirements.original: This type can also be referenced as _MapValueType.from._
requirements.canonical: The type `set of` A of the key set of a map type MapValueType defined as `map from` A `to` B MAY be referenced as MapValueType.from.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.15.5 -- This type can also be referenced as _MapValueType.from._

requirements.original: There is always exactly one value mapped to each key in a map value.
requirements.canonical: In a map value, exactly one value IS mapped to each key.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.15.5 -- There is always exactly one value mapped to each key in a map value.

requirements.original: The values in the set of keys are always unique, so comparing two values from the set of keys that have a different index using the equality operator will always yield false.
requirements.canonical: Each value in the set of keys of a map value IS unique.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.15.5 -- The values in the set of keys are always unique, so comparing two values from the set of keys that have a different index using the equality operator will always yield false.

requirements.original: The values in the set of keys are always unique, so comparing two values from the set of keys that have a different index using the equality operator will always yield false.
requirements.canonical: Comparing two elements with different indices of the set of keys of a map value using the equality operator IS always false.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.15.5 -- The values in the set of keys are always unique, so comparing two values from the set of keys that have a different index using the equality operator will always yield false.

requirements.original: Since the length of the map value is equal to the number of key value pairs in the map value and there is precisely one key per value, the length of the set of keys is equal to the length of the map value.
requirements.canonical: The length of the set of keys of a map value IS equal to the length of the map value, i.e. the number of key value pairs.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.15.5 -- Since the length of the map value is equal to the number of key value pairs in the map value and there is precisely one key per value, the length of the set of keys is equal to the length of the map value.

requirements.original: The set of values that the map contains can be accessed using the to selector.
requirements.canonical: The set of values that a map contains MAY be accessed using the `to` selector.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.15.6 -- The set of values that the map contains can be accessed using the to selector.

requirements.original: MapValue "." to
requirements.canonical: The `to` selector on a map value has the syntax MapValue "." `to`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.15.6 -- MapValue "." to

requirements.original: MapValueType "." `to`
requirements.canonical: The `to` selector on a map type has the syntax MapValueType "." `to`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.15.6 -- MapValueType "." `to`

requirements.original: If MapValue is a value of type MapValueType defined as map `from` _A_ `to` _B then MapValue.to yields a result_ compatible with type set of _B that contains all the values from MapValue.
requirements.canonical: If MapValue is a value of a type defined as `map from` A `to` B, then MapValue.to yields a result compatible with type `set of` B that contains all values of MapValue.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.15.6 -- If MapValue is a value of type MapValueType defined as map `from` _A_ `to` _B then MapValue.to yields a result_ compatible with type set of _B that contains all the values from MapValue.

requirements.original: This type can also be referenced as_ _MapValueType.to;_
requirements.canonical: The type `set of` B of the value set of a map type MapValueType defined as `map from` A `to` B MAY be referenced as MapValueType.to.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.15.6 -- This type can also be referenced as_ _MapValueType.to;_

requirements.original: Since two different keys might be mapped to the same value in a map value, the values in the set of values might not be unique.
requirements.canonical: The set of values of a map value CAN contain duplicate values, because two different keys can be mapped to the same value.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.15.6 -- Since two different keys might be mapped to the same value in a map value, the values in the set of values might not be unique.

requirements.original: The set of values will contain one value for each key value pair in the map.
requirements.canonical: The set of values of a map value IS composed of exactly one value for each key value pair in the map.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.15.6 -- The set of values will contain one value for each key value pair in the map.

requirements.original: Since the length of the map value is equal to number of key value pairs in the map value and there is precisely one item for each key value pair in the set of values, the length of the set of values is equal to the length of map value.
requirements.canonical: The length of the set of values of a map value IS equal to the length of the map value, i.e. the number of key value pairs.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.15.6 -- Since the length of the map value is equal to number of key value pairs in the map value and there is precisely one item for each key value pair in the set of values, the length of the set of values is equal to the length of map value.

requirements.original: When referencing an element of an uninitialized map value or field or omitted field (including omitting a field at a higher level of the embedding hierarchy) on the left-hand side of an assignment, the reference shall recursively be expanded up to and including the depth of the referenced element as follows:
requirements.canonical: When an element of an uninitialized or omitted map value or field is referenced on the left hand side of an assignment, the reference SHALL be recursively expanded up to and including the depth of the referenced element.
requirements.condition: an element of an uninitialized map value, field or omitted field is referenced on the left hand side of an assignment
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.15.7 -- When referencing an element of an uninitialized map value or field or omitted field (including omitting a field at a higher level of the embedding hierarchy) on the left-hand side of an assignment, the reference shall recursively be expanded up to and including the depth of the referenced element as follows:

requirements.original: a) When expanding a value or value field of map type, the element referenced by the index notation shall be set to present.
requirements.canonical: When a value or value field of map type is expanded, the element referenced by the index notation SHALL be set to present.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.15.7 -- a) When expanding a value or value field of map type, the element referenced by the index notation shall be set to present.

requirements.original: b) Expansion of record, record of and set of, union and set values and intermediate fields shall follow the rules of item a) in clauses 6.2.1.1, 6.2.3.0 and 6.2.5.1 and clause 6.2.2.1 correspondingly.
requirements.canonical: During expansion of a map reference, expansion of record, record of, set of, union and set values and intermediate fields SHALL follow item a) of clauses 6.2.1.1, 6.2.3.0, 6.2.5.1 and 6.2.2.1 respectively.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.15.7 -- b) Expansion of record, record of and set of, union and set values and intermediate fields shall follow the rules of item a) in clauses 6.2.1.1, 6.2.3.0 and 6.2.5.1 and clause 6.2.2.1 correspondingly.

requirements.original: c) At the end of the expansion, the value at the right-hand side of the assignment shall be assigned to the referenced element.
requirements.canonical: At the end of the expansion, the value on the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be assigned to the referenced element.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.15.7 -- c) At the end of the expansion, the value at the right-hand side of the assignment shall be assigned to the referenced element.

requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports the definition of map types with nested structured types for the to part.
requirements.canonical: A map type MAY have a nested structured type as its value (`to`) type.

examples.text: type map from charstring to map from charstring to charstring MapType;

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.15.8 -- TTCN-3 supports the definition of map types with nested structured types for the to part.

requirements.original: The usage of structured types (record, set, enumerated, set `of, record` `of, union and map) is allowed.`
requirements.canonical: The value (`to`) type of a map type MAY be a record, set, enumerated, set of, record of, union or map type.

ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether the permission of structured types applies only to the 'to' part (as the preceding sentence says) or also to the key type (the NOTE implies structured keys are allowed but discouraged). The 'to'-only reading is used here.
readings: The value (to) type of a map type MAY be a structured type.
Both the key (from) type and the value (to) type of a map type MAY be structured types.

examples.text: type map from charstring to map from charstring to charstring MapType;

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.15.8 -- The usage of structured types (record, set, enumerated, set `of, record` `of, union and map) is allowed.`

requirements.original: In map values, both keys and value fields associated with them are mandatory.
requirements.canonical: In a map value, each key and its associated value field IS mandatory.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.15.9 -- In map values, both keys and value fields associated with them are mandatory.

requirements.original: The omit symbol shall not be assigned to a map key or value field.
requirements.canonical: The `omit` symbol SHALL NOT be assigned to a map key or to a map value field.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.15.9 -- The omit symbol shall not be assigned to a map key or value field.

requirements.original: Keys of map templates shall not contain matching symbols.
requirements.canonical: A key of a map template SHALL NOT contain matching symbols.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.15.9 -- Keys of map templates shall not contain matching symbols.

requirements.original: Value fields associated with keys of map templates might contain matching symbols including symbols for optional fields such as omit, * or ifpresent (see Annex B for more details).
requirements.canonical: A value field associated with a key of a map template MAY contain matching symbols, including `omit`, `*` and `ifpresent`.

ambiguity.issue: 6.2.15.9-s002 forbids assigning omit to a map value field, while this sentence allows omit, * and ifpresent in map template value fields; also 'might' can be read as permission or as possibility. The permission reading for templates is used.
readings: A value field of a map template MAY contain omit, * or ifpresent.
A value field of a map template MAY contain matching symbols, but omit (and therefore * / ifpresent with omit semantics) is excluded by the prohibition of omit for map value fields.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.15.9 -- Value fields associated with keys of map templates might contain matching symbols including symbols for optional fields such as omit, * or ifpresent (see Annex B for more details).

requirements.original: Values of all types can be directly passed as actual parameters to formal parameters of the open type without the need to explicitly specify a type context.
requirements.canonical: A value of any type MAY be passed directly as an actual parameter to a formal parameter of the open type without explicitly specifying a type context.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.16 -- Values of all types can be directly passed as actual parameters to formal parameters of the open type without the need to explicitly specify a type context.

requirements.original: a) The open type shall be used only in formal parameter of predefined or external functions.
requirements.canonical: The open type SHALL only be used as the type of a formal parameter of a predefined or external function.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.16 -- a) The open type shall be used only in formal parameter of predefined or external functions.

requirements.original: Type declarations
requirements.canonical: The open type SHALL NOT be used in a type declaration.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.16 -- Type declarations

requirements.original: Variable declarations
requirements.canonical: The open type SHALL NOT be used in a variable declaration.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.16 -- Variable declarations

requirements.original: Template declarations
requirements.canonical: The open type SHALL NOT be used in a template declaration.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.16 -- Template declarations

requirements.original: Constant declarations
requirements.canonical: The open type SHALL NOT be used in a constant declaration.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.16 -- Constant declarations

requirements.original: Module parameter declarations
requirements.canonical: The open type SHALL NOT be used in a module parameter declaration.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.16 -- Module parameter declarations

requirements.original: Formal parameters of templates, test cases, altsteps, non-external functions, map and unmap operations
requirements.canonical: The open type SHALL NOT be used as the type of a formal parameter of a template, testcase, altstep, non-external function, map operation or unmap operation.

ambiguity.issue: 'map and unmap operations' may denote the port map/unmap operations (which have a param clause) or the map type unmap statement of clause 6.2.15.3. The port operation reading is used.
readings: The open type SHALL NOT be used in the param clause of the port map and unmap operations.
The open type SHALL NOT be used as an argument type of the unmap statement on map variables (clause 6.2.15.3).

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.16 -- Formal parameters of templates, test cases, altsteps, non-external functions, map and unmap operations

requirements.original: Return clauses of functions
requirements.canonical: The open type SHALL NOT be used in the return clause of a function.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.16 -- Return clauses of functions

requirements.original: Generally, TTCN-3 requires type compatibility of values at assignments, instantiations and comparison.
requirements.canonical: A value used in an assignment, an instantiation or a comparison SHALL be type compatible with the type of the target or of the other operand.

ambiguity.issue: 'Generally' implies exceptions without listing them here; the exceptions (strong typing) are given in clause 6.3.4. Chose the reading that type compatibility is the default rule.
readings: A value used in an assignment, an instantiation or a comparison SHALL be type compatible with the target type, except where clause 6.3.4 requires strong typing.
A value used in an assignment, an instantiation or a comparison SHALL be type compatible with the target type in all cases.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.3.0 -- Generally, TTCN-3 requires type compatibility of values at assignments, instantiations and comparison.

requirements.original: NOTE: As address is more a predefined type name than a distinct type with its own properties, the same type compatibility rules apply to an address type and to its derivatives as the rules were if the type was defined with a name different from address.
requirements.canonical: An `address` type and its derivatives ARE subject to the same type compatibility rules as a type with the same definition but a name different from `address`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.3.0 -- NOTE: As address is more a predefined type name than a distinct type with its own properties, the same type compatibility rules apply to an address type and to its derivatives as the rules were if the type was defined with a name different from address.

requirements.original: For variables, constants, templates, etc. of simple basic types and basic string types the value "b" is compatible to type "A" if type "B" resolves to the same root type as type "A" (e.g. integer) and it does not violate subtyping (e.g. ranges, length restrictions) of type "A".
requirements.canonical: A value "b" of a simple basic type or basic string type IS compatible with type "A" if type "B" resolves to the same root type as type "A" and value "b" does not violate the subtyping (e.g. ranges, length restrictions) of type "A".
requirements.condition: type "B" is a simple basic type or basic string type
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.3.1 -- For variables, constants, templates, etc. of simple basic types and basic string types the value "b" is compatible to type "A" if type "B" resolves to the same root type as type "A" (e.g. integer) and it does not violate subtyping (e.g. ranges, length restrictions) of type "A".

requirements.original: For variables, constants, templates, etc. of charstring type, value 'b' is compatible with a universal charstring type 'A' unless it violates any type constraint specification (range, list or length) of type "A".
requirements.canonical: A value "b" of charstring type IS compatible with a universal charstring type "A" unless value "b" violates a type constraint specification (range, list or length) of type "A".
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.3.1 -- For variables, constants, templates, etc. of charstring type, value 'b' is compatible with a universal charstring type 'A' unless it violates any type constraint specification (range, list or length) of type "A".

requirements.original: For variables, constants, templates, etc. of universal charstring type, value 'b' is compatible with a charstring type 'A' if all characters used in value 'b' have their corresponding characters (i.e. the same control or graphical character using the same character code) in the type charstring and it does not violate any type constraint specification (range, list or length) of type "A".
requirements.canonical: A value "b" of universal charstring type IS compatible with a charstring type "A" if every character of value "b" has a corresponding character (the same control or graphical character with the same character code) in the charstring type and value "b" does not violate a type constraint specification (range, list or length) of type "A".
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.3.1 -- For variables, constants, templates, etc. of universal charstring type, value 'b' is compatible with a charstring type 'A' if all characters used in value 'b' have their corresponding characters (i.e. the same control or graphical character using the same character code) in the type charstring and it does not violate any type constraint specification (range, list or length) of type "A".
